why: 32:2 ends 'saying,' and 32:5 opens 'Wherefore, said they' with nothing said; restore 32:4 (the land is good for cattle, and we have cattle) and drop 32:7, whose question 32:6 and 32:8 already carry
Deut 17 opens at 17:6 with 'he that is worthy of death', but the idolater being judged (17:2-5) is never mentioned

bridges.Deuteronomy 17:6: Anyone found worshipping other gods is to be stoned to death, but only on sound testimony.

why: 21:11 'And seest among the captives' begins mid-sentence with no war or captives in view; restore 21:10 and drop the minor mixed-fabric rule 22:11 (22:10 still stands alone)
23:14 'For the LORD walketh in the midst of thy camp ... that he see no unclean thing' follows the Edomite rule and explains nothing the reader saw (the camp-cleanliness law 23:12-13 is dropped)

bridges.Deuteronomy 23:14: Soldiers are to keep the war camp clean, burying their waste outside it.

why: Jeshurun appears at 32:15 unintroduced, and 'waxed fat' follows nothing since God's feeding of Israel (32:13-14) is dropped

bridges.Deuteronomy 32:15: God feeds Israel, here poetically called Jeshurun, on the richest food of the land.

why: 8:14 'when the king of Ai saw it' points at nothing: the main army's open advance on Ai (8:10-13) is dropped

bridges.Joshua 8:14: Next morning Joshua marches the main army up openly and camps in sight of Ai, while the ambush waits behind the city.

why: 10:1 is an unfinished 'when ... had heard' clause and 10:3 'Wherefore' has nothing to follow from; restore 10:2 (they feared greatly, for Gibeon was a great city) and drop 10:7, which 10:9 makes redundant
11:1 breaks off mid-list of kings and 11:4 'And they went out' has no clear subject beyond three named kings

bridges.Joshua 11:4: He summons every king of northern Canaan to join him against Israel.

why: 12:24 'The king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty and one' reads as a stray fragment after 12:7 announces the list

bridges.Joshua 12:24: Thirty-one conquered kings are listed city by city, from Jericho and Ai onward.

why: 20:2 'Speak to the children of Israel' has no speaker (20:1 'The LORD also spake unto Joshua' dropped); restore it and drop the border description 1:4, whose loss leaves 1:3 to 1:5 intact

22:13 ends 'Phinehas ... the priest,' and 22:16 opens 'Thus saith the whole congregation' mid-sentence; restore 22:15 ('they came ... and spake with them, saying') and drop 24:12, whose 'two kings of the Amorites' confuses the Jericho summary

Ehud brings the present at 3:17 and then 3:19 'But he himself turned again' makes no sense without 3:18 (he sent the bearers away); restore it and drop the lone-verse tribal note 1:34 at the end of a highlight-reel run

In the song, Sisera's mother asks why he is late (5:28) and 5:30 'Have they not sped?' answers with no signal of who speaks; restore 5:29 (her wise ladies answered) and drop 5:3, whose loss leaves 5:2 to 5:4 smooth
8:27 'made an ephod thereof' refers to gold the reader never sees handed over (8:25-26 dropped)

bridges.Judges 8:27: The men gladly throw their gold earrings onto a spread garment, about seventeen hundred shekels of gold.
